children: bipartisan permitting reform legislation Thursday designed to speed up energy, mining, and other infrastructure projects and marking the closest that Congress has come to overhauling the federal permitting system in years.

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act aims to streamline federal permitting by shortening the deadlines for many environmental reviews, reducing the window to sue developers over certain environmental concerns, and restricting the circumstances for withdrawing approvals on projects.

Supporters of the bill say multiyear wait times and burdensome environmental laws make infrastructure projects more expensive by introducing uncertainty and regulatory risk, adding to costs for consumers, while environmental advocates and Native American tribes say the bill would weaken environmental protection laws and benefit fossil fuel companies.

The issue of project bottlenecks that raise costs for ​consumers and ⁠businesses has taken on urgency as AI's rapid growth drives electricity demand, raising concerns about power prices and whether the grid can expand quickly to support new data centers.
The House will pick up the bill when it returns from its Thanksgiving break, and President Trump has said he ​will sign the bill into law, but passage in the House is far from certain.

While 14 Democrats and one independent who caucuses with Democrats joined 47 Republicans in voting for the bill, more Democrats in the House have been vocal about pushing negotiations to the next Congress, when they will hold large majorities in both chambers.
Some Republicans who lost their seats in the recent midterm elections may not return after the holidays, and the House still must pass government funding and the National Defense Authorization Act.

title: Senate passes bipartisan bill to cut permitting times for energy projects; House to vote next month
